title: Regulation of proton transference for stable and efficient reactive capture of CO2 from air - Nature Energy
byline: Liu; Hengzhou; Shin; Heejong; Yuyin; Su; Guangcan; Peng; Bosi; Wang; Yong; Huang; Jianan Erick; Song; Ji-Yoon; Zhou; Bei; Chen; Yuanjun; An; Hongmin; Ze; Huajie
html:
Abstract

Direct air capture combined with electrosynthesis could turn atmospheric CO2 into fuels, but releasing tightly bound CO2 from capture liquids demands intense heat, and the resulting end-to-end energy burden exceeds 35 GJ per tonne of CO. Electrified reactive capture avoids thermal regeneration by feeding capture liquid directly into an electrolyser, yet reported systems remain energy-intensive and typically fail within 100 h. Here we show that these failures trace to proton management: too large a flux of protons crossing the membrane acidifies the cathode and degrades the catalyst, while too small a flux starves proton-driven in situ CO2 release, both favouring hydrogen evolution. We define the proton transference number (\({{{t}}}_{{{\rm{H}}}^{+}}\)), the fraction of ionic current carried by protons, as a quantitative descriptor linking ion transport to CO selectivity, carbon utilization and durability. Replacing oxygen evolution with gas-fed hydrogen oxidation at the anode maintains \({{{t}}}_{{{\rm{H}}}^{+}}\approx 1\), enabling 1,000 h of stable operation at ~1 V and 100 mA cm−2, and CO production from air at 22 GJ t−1 with >90% carbon utilization.
